content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.1) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.27–0.44), model often overreacts with a sharp upward bias — reduce forecast slope.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates mid-term peaks (e.g., 72–74) — cap forecast at 73.5 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 74, model often forecasts a sharp drop — reverse this by adding 0.5–1.0 to forecast if sentiment > 0.4.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low but price is trending up — add 0.3–0.7 to forecast if sentiment < 0.1 and price > 70.5.
- Avoid forecasting spikes if sentiment is flat or negative — model tends to overreact to minor sentiment shifts.
